St. Raphael of Brooklyn

Saints

St. Raphael of Brooklyn

St. Raphael Hawaweeny · St. Rafla Hawawini

Period
1860–1915
Region
North America
Titles / vocation
Hierarch · Missionary
Commemoration
February 27

Introduction

St. Raphael Hawaweeny is the missionary bishop who gathered Arabic-speaking Orthodox communities throughout North America.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Repose following heart illness, February 14/27, 1915.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA describes birth to Syrian parents and education at Damascus, Halki, and Kyiv before teaching and ecclesiastical work in Russia.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 3; Published biographical account,paragraph 6; Published biographical account,paragraph 8; Published biographical account,paragraph 12

The DECR’s biographical note connects Raphael’s family to displacement from Damascus to Beirut, and follows the return to Syria, education at Halki, and subsequent work in Russia. It records his Arabic teaching at Kazan before the American ministry. The sequence supplies geographic background to a bishop whose later flock likewise crossed languages and borders.

[2] Official commemoration report with biographical note · DECR report of29February2024 and biographical note,paragraph 6; DECR report of29February2024 and biographical note,paragraph 7; DECR report of29February2024 and biographical note,paragraph 11

Life and notable events

He reaches New York in 1895 and travels widely to organize communities, provide clergy, and publish Arabic church material.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 12; Published biographical account,paragraph 14; Published biographical account,paragraph 15; Published biographical account,paragraph 18

The OCA describes practical provision for communities without church buildings: visits to scattered families, training or recruitment of clergy, and an Arabic service book. It also records his interest in usable English translations for worship and instruction. These details make clear that missionary work included sustained pastoral organization and publishing, as well as travel and the establishment of parishes.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 18; Published biographical account,paragraph 21; Published biographical account,paragraph 30; Published biographical account,paragraph 35

Death and martyrdom

The official life records heart illness and repose on February 14/27, 1915. It is a death from illness, not a martyrdom account.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 34; Published biographical account,paragraph 35

Writings and legacy

At his repose the mission numbered thirty parishes. The OCA notes his scholarship, The Word, and support for English in services and education.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 36; Published biographical account,paragraph 37

I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;

Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.

For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;

And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.

But watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry.

For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.

I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:

Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.

The OCA explicitly applies2Timothy4: 5 to Raphael’s pastoral labors. This quotation supplies that passage’s surrounding biblical context, not a new liturgical assignment.

[3] Public-domain Bible translation · 2 Timothy 4: 1–8

The report records his 2000 canonization by the OCA and glorification at St.Tikhon’s Monastery. It then documents his February 2024 commemoration at Moscow’s OCA representation, with Metropolitan Niphon of the Antiochian Church presiding. This is a specific dated instance of later veneration, not a claim that all Orthodox jurisdictions use one identical annual commemoration.

[2] Official commemoration report with biographical note · DECR report of29February2024 and biographical note,paragraph 1; DECR report of29February2024 and biographical note,paragraph 2; DECR report of29February2024 and biographical note,paragraph 9; DECR report of29February2024 and biographical note,paragraph 13
